OWASP Top 10:2021 application weaknesses (SEC-01..SEC-20) in agmws-*/agmbo-* sources: injection-shaped SQL/command/LDAP composition, path containment, missing authorization and test/bypass endpoints, error detail in responses, sensitive logging, weak cryptography, token validation/issuance, TLS bypass, unsafe deserialization, permissive CORS, method override, open redirect, sensitive query values, secret/personal response fields, unbounded paging and host security headers. Lexical review candidates only; Golden-backed classes (CTL-03, data access, error and logging rules) report tier MUST, the rest are a package security baseline (SHOULD) and never a Golden verdict.

Same SEC classes for AgriMap.Platform, without controller authorization and host-header checks: shared auth, crypto, serialization, storage and HTTP helpers are where many of these defaults live, so a finding here can reach every consumer service.

Angular DOM XSS sinks and sanitizer bypass (SEC-21), tokens in Web Storage (SEC-22), redirects from return/query values (SEC-15) and credentials in URL query strings (SEC-16) in agmwa-* TypeScript. External .html templates are not selected, so template bindings there are not assessed.
Same frontend SEC classes for @agrimap/* libraries; a published helper that writes HTML or stores tokens affects every consuming app.

Dynamic SQL (EXEC(@sql), EXEC with concatenation, sp_executesql over concatenated text) that is not parameterized or QUOTENAME-protected (SEC-01). Variables assembled in another object stay unknown and are reported as candidates.

Needs data-flow or runtime evidence: object-level authorization (IDOR / API1:2023), mass assignment, CSRF on cookie-authenticated endpoints, SSRF (A10:2021) from caller-supplied URLs, file-upload content validation and rate limiting.
A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components needs package manifests matched against an advisory database (SCA). Lint reads no NuGet/npm advisory data and does not claim component safety.

Owned by the server, container, reverse proxy or gateway rather than application source: HTTP request smuggling (CL/TE handling), unpatched web servers, TLS cipher suites, internal IP or server banners in proxy responses, OPTIONS/TRACE method exposure and open database or OS ports. Public-Key-Pins (HPKP) is deprecated by browsers and deliberately not adopted; HSTS is checked instead (SEC-19).
